chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Suwayd, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'I am being tested with looking at a beautiful woman, and looking at her fascinates me.' He said to me: 'O Ali! There is no harm if Allah recognizes sincerity from your intention, and beware of adultery, for it obliterates blessings and destroys the religion.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on looking at a beautiful woman in Islam according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the natural act of looking (al-nazar) and the internal state of the heart, permitting it provided one guards against the transition to adultery (al-zina). He emphasizes that while the physical act is not inherently sinful, adultery is spiritually destructive as it 'eradicates blessings' (yamhaq al-baraka) and consumes one's faith. This reflects the Shia scholarly focus on intention (niyyah) and the gradual progression from permissible acts to major sins through unchecked desire.
